messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Adding Methods to Compiled Models
parts:
In order to finish refactoring the command io I need to add some methods to the models, but I don't know how to modify stanc appropriately so that the methods are auto generated correctly. Can anyone provide an example?

The methods should be straightforward to implement,

string get_model_name()
void get_constrained_param_names(vector<string>& v)
void get_unconstrained_param_names(vector<string>& v)
void get_constained_values(vector<double>& v, const vector<double>& r, const vector<int>& i)

P.S. Attached is an example of the preliminary graphical diagnostics the refactoring admits.

This is an excellent idea. I've been meaning to refactor
along these lines for ages to make external interfaces
easier.

The examples are all buried in gm/generator.hpp,
which is the ugliest file of code in all of Stan :-(

The method write_array() is generated for the vector-based version
of write_csv() that does the real parameter part of your
get_constrained_values.

What is v? Are you getting gradients? If so, I'd
suggest a more suggestive function name (do what I
say, not what I did!).

Daniel and I are going to code review and refactor
all of generator. We can do that next week and
use the implementation of your methods as a running
example and have it done by the end of the week.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Adding Methods to Compiled Models
parts:
Two issues.

1. What should the unconstrained param names be?

They're not in 1-1 correspondence with

type constrained unconstrained
simplex K K-1
corr_matrix K*K (K choose 2)
cov_matrix K*K K + (K choose 2)

corr_matrix (K choose 2 vs. K*K), cov_matrix (K + K choose 2
vs. K*K). [I'm guessing the unit-length normed variables behave
like simplex, but I haven't looked that closely.]

Can I just dump out the name and then the index in the
unconstrained vector? So every name would be either
"foo" or "foo.<N>", where <N> is the param index (indexing
from 1, of course).

2. There's an issue with how things are currently organized
that's making it hard for me to give Michael the method he
wants:

- void get_constrained_values(vector<double>& v, const vector<double>& r, const vector<int>& i)

The problem is that the unconstrained parameters r aren't quite
enough to generate all the output values because there's potentially
RNG involved in the generated quantities block. I had assumed
that the write method would just be called once and in so
doing generates the random quantities.

There's currently a method on models that does what you want:

template <typename RNG>
void write_array(RNG& base_rng__, // in
std::vector<double>& params_r_constrained__, // in
std::vector<int>& params_i__, // in
std::vector<double>& params_r_unconstrained__, // out
std::ostream* pstream__ = 0); // out (optional)

KEY:

v == vars__
r == params_r__
i == params_i__

The RNG base_rng__ is used to generate the random quantities that
might be needed in generated quantities. Are you OK passing
an RNG in?

Also, passing the pstream in for error reporting?

After the above method is called, the params_r_unconstrained__ vector
will contain the values of parameters, transformed parameters, and
generated quantities, in the same order as they are printed.

We can rename this method to be consistent.

The write_csv method is similar, but writes directly to a CSV
file instead of populating an array. I'm eventually going to change
the implementation of write_csv to collect up an array by calling
write_array (or get_constrained_values) and then printing what
comes out to the print stream.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Adding Methods to Compiled Models
parts:
1) Yeah, just so long as you add "unconstrained" or some short-hand to the beginning of each variable. The indexing is exactly what Dan did in the graphical_diagnostic branch.
2) I'm happy taking in error streams (is this our go-to error policy now? If it is I'll need to update mcmc), but the RNG sounds nasty and, honestly, they're not very handy for diagnostics. is it possible to just print out the model parameters and not the generated quantities?

I'm also thinking that we abstract the writing out of model with the mcmc_writer (or some other writer). That way we can have the single writer be responsible for converting arrays of things (whether they be model output or diagnostic output) into csv, json, etc.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Adding Methods to Compiled Models
parts:
On 4/24/13 4:52 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> 1) Yeah, just so long as you add "unconstrained" or some short-hand to the beginning of each variable.
OK. How about just "unc_"?
> The indexing is exactly what Dan did in the graphical_diagnostic branch.
It's the way the code wants to split :-)
> 2) I'm happy taking in error streams (is this our go-to error policy now? If it is I'll need to update mcmc),

Until someone figures out a better way to do it.

We need some way of printing messages back to the
user. We can provide an R stream from R and
a console stream from the command. You can also supply
0 and then there's no error message writing.
> but the RNG sounds nasty and, honestly, they're not very handy for diagnostics. is it possible to just print out the model parameters and not the generated quantities?

Of course. We should think about how to segment this.

For names, we can just have three methods:

parameter_names(vector<string>&);

? transformed_parameter_names(vector<string>&);
? generated_quantities_names(vector<string>&);

all_variable_names(vector<string>&);

For values, the transformed parameters depend on the params,
and the generated quantities depend on both params and
transformed params. And the generated quantities require
an RNG. For parameters, we only really need:

constrain_parameter(const vector<double>& unconstrained_params,
vector<double>& constrained_params);

and then the full one we have now.

> I'm also thinking that we abstract the writing out of model with the mcmc_writer (or some other writer).

> That way we can have the single writer be responsible for converting arrays of
> things (whether they be model output or diagnostic output) into csv, json, etc.

We've abstracted input that way in the var_context class.
It would totally make sense to do that with output. We'd
need to define a var_writer base class to match var_context (which
should be renamed var_reader, I think).

Then we'd have to implement a concrete instance to write out to arrays.

The question is which methods do we need?

I'll just implement the only-params array version for you now while
I design the interfaces for the more abstracted approach.

- Bob

- Bob
